steps.text: confirm the hooks are wired as install would write them: coherence hooks --check --host <claude or codex>

make your first message to the user, before any other step, how Coherence works, in your own words and within one screen, from docs/how-coherence-works.md in the installed package (an agent that explained last, beside its questions, left the user watching nothing while it worked): lead with what an invariant is, what must stay true from one version of their system to the next however much the code around it changes, then the five moments of a session and what Coherence does at each, then what a component, a requirement, an enforcement, a refutation, an entrance and a spec gap are, and what a short set of invariants buys them; call each one an invariant, never a rule; say that you will propose the invariants for them to confirm, and invite their questions; put it where the user reads it whole, since some agent hosts fold text written before a question tool into one line

in that same first message, give them Scope to watch while you work: start coherence scope from the project's own folder (the adopted folder in a monorepo), kept running, and give its address; its Home shows the project as its files, and each spec you write gathers its folder's files into a component they can see; only then go on to the config
steps.leaves: Scope's address in the first message, or that the user declined

steps.text: write coherence.config.json where the project lives: at the repository root for a whole repository; in a monorepo, in the folder you adopt, after coherence adopt <folder> from the root when the repository keeps a registry (a root config with projects), writing only the keys the folder overrides; name, language (a list when the folder spans Python and TypeScript, the first the primary), the folders that are not this project's code or prose under ignore (vendored code, generated output, fixtures), and, where the project has tests, test with testMatch and testJson, or tests, one setup per runner with its own cwd; every key is in docs/config.md in the installed package
settle the vocabulary: coherence lexicon coverage, then declare the terms that carry the project's meaning (the practice settle a domain term)

to settle one part of the project first, name its folders or files: coherence lexicon coverage src/billing docs, and coherence lexicon draft src/billing for its unsettled candidates; each path is relative to the root or absolute inside it, and the config's ignore list still holds inside it

where the repository already declares its module boundaries in a file coherence scaffold import reads (tach.toml today), draft the component specs from it first: coherence scaffold import tach --all prints one draft per module with its dependencies and exposed paths as bullets, and --write creates only the specs that do not exist; fill each placeholder (where tach enforces a drafted facade, the chokepoint is graded checker-choked by tach itself, so its own check is the enforcement), and place the via: tests it prints where the project's tests run
steps.leaves: the drafted specs, listed by --write as wrote or skipped

steps.text: declare the components and where work enters them: the entry spec with its trust levels, one spec per component folder, then the entrances coherence scaffold entrances ranks first, 10 to 20 of them and every one carrying outside trust in whose handler writes, a family that goes through one helper as one grouped entrance, and the rest left undeclared (the practice declare entrances); the grammar is in docs/spec.md in the installed package

give each real unit its own spec at whatever depth it sits, not one per top-level folder: run coherence mass, and for each folder it names as having no spec of its own, write its spec or declare it under ## folded in the spec of the component above, with why it belongs there (docs/spec.md, Folded folders); repeat until mass names none
steps.leaves: mass names no folder with no spec of its own

steps.text: declare the few invariants that matter most (security, tenant isolation, data integrity), each through the practice declare a requirement, proposing each to the user first in plain words: the invariant, what goes wrong for the project if it breaks, and how it would be checked; for a module boundary whose own code may use its internals, say which references the chokepoint governs (from: outside the component), and in a folder of a larger repository, where the boundary's callers live outside it, choose the references horizon in the config (a list of folders, or repository)

run, then witness each refutation (the practice witness a refutation); a broken chokepoint is a finding to report with its bypass sites, not a failure to hide; a requirement the code already breaks stays a requirement, with a defect per site and an escalation, and a test that cannot run here is recorded as unable
baseline what the project already held: coherence lexicon baseline, and coherence scaffold control --baseline for entrances with no traced control
steps.leaves: the baseline records in the journal

steps.text: find the methods the project already has (the practice harvest practices)

ask the user how Coherence should run on pull requests, presenting both modes: fail (the check fails on a spec problem or a structural defect) or comment (one report comment on the pull request, updated on each push, and the check fails only when Coherence itself breaks); then run coherence ci install --host github --mode <their choice> --write, or record with decide that they declined

commit coherence.config.json (and the registry's change, when adopt wrote one), the lexicon, the specs and practice files, the hook settings unless they were installed --local (when .gitignore keeps them out of git, add an exception for that one file, such as !.claude/settings.json, unless the user strongly prefers otherwise: the hooks are how Coherence reaches every session in the project, and a teammate's agent without them gets no vocabulary, specs, journal or checks), the CI workflow, .coherence/.gitignore (hooks install wrote it so git sees nothing Coherence regenerates), and .coherence/journal, .coherence/runs and .coherence/work

report what Scope's Home now says, in its own terms and with no verdict over the whole project: how many components the project has, how many invariants guard how many of them and how old the checks behind them are, any invariant whose last check failed, broken chokepoints, entrances with no traced control, how many detected entrances stay undeclared (a count, no finding), and components no enforcement covers; open Scope from the project's own folder if it is not open, and point the user at Home's replay of how the project took shape

Scope failed when run from an adopter's own folder, because every page until then had been built from Coherence's checkout with --root (d-01976691)
a coverage report redirected into the adopter's root was read back as its source and grew on every run (df-79ac2d4e)
both outside adoptions left their route gaps open because nothing in the session's loop showed them (d-a1095ef2)

an adoption declared one spec per top-level folder and stopped, and a human had to ask for the nested units (df-9750aee2)
three trial adoptions of umami, whose .gitignore excludes .claude, each stopped at the commit to ask whether the hook settings should be committed (d-58daa53f)
an adoption recorded seven decisions for the 69 folders that belonged to the component above, and mass, which reads no decision, still named all 69 (d-8ebb2e2e)
a fresh adoption found its first requirements already false and its tests unable to run unattended, and had to improvise what to record (df-8ac95c4d)

in a monorepo, a session started at the repository root took the whole repository as the project: another team's specs reached orient, their practices fired, and .coherence was written at the root (df-0b68c987)
a chokepoint in a project nested below the repository top passed without searching the rest of the repository, where a product boundary's bypasses live; choose its references horizon (df-0d235229)
the user was asked which invariants to declare before anything had said what an invariant is, or what Coherence does with one (df-729d4e68)
